definition: 1.5 Hz, 50 % duty, generated in the PMU. `hazard` = A8 == HAZARD \|\| A8 == HAZ+HORN. Hazard overrides the stalk and works with the key out

A15 entering HEAD, or leaving HEAD, or A8 == WINK_L / WINK_R with A16 <= ACC → energise O1 until the transit bit clears on BOTH sides (A4 in IDLE/CRANK_OK and A5 in IDLE/REVERSE), minimum 300 ms. 4 s with either still showing transit = obstruction: O1 off, fault flag. A held wink switch opens the OTHER side's relay coil return, so only the winked lamp moves. D-460 (2026-10-09): the motors are driven the Mazda way - O1 feeds WR and K1 / K2 steer 12 V to R (up) or RY (down); each motor runs only while its command disagrees with its cam and stops itself at the end (SP-584), so O1 on with the lamps already where they are commanded moves nothing. What holds K1 / K2 in up, and how transit is sensed now that YG is +12 V while running, wait on the blocks drafted by R-APPLY-01.16; until then the transit terms above are the old ladder's

When the stalk goes to OFF with the wipers running, hold O8 until A3 reads PARKED (or BRAKE+PARKED), then release — braking stops the arm at park. Intermittent: 3 s pause between full sweeps, each sweep runs until PARKED. One-touch: LOW held < 400 ms → one sweep to PARKED (D-225)
WASH also holds O8 on; K12 closes only while the stalk contact is pressed, so the pump runs only while the driver holds WASH. After release, keep O8 on for two more sweeps
O21 only in P or N — the inhibitor bit alone, whether or not the left pop-up happens to be in transit (D-240): A4 == CRANK_OK or TRANSIT+PN. Release O21 when A16 leaves START
Refuse a new pop-up command while O1 reads above 20 A

Warn below 12.0 V. Shed COMFORT, INTERIOR, ACCESSORY and DEFOG only after about 10 s continuously below 11.5 V, never while A16 == START (cranking sags to about 10.5 V), and restore them only once the supply is back above about 12.0 V - 0.5 V of hysteresis (D-463, amending D-248's undelayed shed; DEFOG added by R11). ACCESSORY (O10) is never shed while the engine runs (ignition_on && oil_ok), so the ICU, its speed sensor and the cluster stay up on a dying alternator; with the engine off it sheds as before. The comfort loads still shed. Warn above 15.0 V. INTERIOR (O20, the dash illumination since D-462) is likewise never shed while the engine runs and sheds with the engine off (D-476).

Split by fault type (D-279). Hard overcurrent: bounded fast retries, then latch, then flag. Open-load or thermal: no latch. NEVER a silent latch on a safety channel — a latched stop lamp or headlamp must annunciate, because a latched-off headlamp at night is worse than a flickering one. Motors trip on a stall timer, not a current spike

Any wake-strip input high wakes the PMU. With no key, no door and nothing on A8, KEEP_ALIVE drops 30 s after the last change and the PMU sleeps; K11 opens with it (audio memory relies on the head unit's own non-volatile memory). A stuck door cannot hold the car awake: with A16 == OFF, KEEP_ALIVE releases after 30 minutes whatever A6 reads (D-248). The hazards are the one exception: while the hazard switch is on (A8 == HAZARD or HAZ+HORN) the car stays awake with no limit, past the 30-minute forced sleep - many hours on the 40 Ah pack, until the pack's protection cuts in (D-464) Confirm on the PMU-24 (R11): whether its wake inputs are level- or edge-sensitive - the bench model wakes on an input going high, so a door left open cannot re-wake the car straight after the forced sleep; if the real PMU wakes on a level, the stuck-door case needs its own rule.

Each output's healthy current is a band around a MEASURED baseline, never a typed figure. `pins.baseline_a` is read live in the client at shakedown (CK01) and the band derives from it: a lamp channel flags below 0.5 x baseline_a and a motor channel above 1.5 x baseline_a. The low half is the PMU's own Min Current parameter, which raises UNDERCURRENT and does NOT switch the output off (D-279) - it is an annunciator and no logic may be built on it. The high half is a written function, not the soft fuse: `enable_a` is unchanged by any of this. The PMU cannot measure below its own floor - about 0.5 A typical and up to 2 A on the 25 A outputs (O1-O5, O12-O16), about 0.2 A on the 15 A outputs (O6-O11), about 0.1 A on the 7 A outputs (O17-O22) - so a channel whose baseline is under four times its floor gets no band at all. O21 at 0.2 A and O22 at 0.2 A are that case and get none.

Every output carries a `logic.retry_class` and the class sets the PMU's Retry count / Retry every / Retry forever fields. D-279 set the policy; this names it so one output cannot quietly differ from its peers. lamp - 3 retries at 5 s, then latch AND annunciate; a safety channel never latches silently. motor - 5 retries at 15 s, no latch; a stall timer governs, not a current spike, because a stalled wiper is a thermal event. critical - 1 retry at 2 s, then off until the key leaves RUN; a fuel pump or an ignition that trips twice is a fault, not a nuisance. guarded - 1 retry, then off and flag: a trip here means something is physically in the way, so retrying is the wrong answer. O1 during a pop-up cycle is the only one, and the D-186 obstruction timeout is its real handler. conditional - the class follows the consumer the PMU last commanded on the channel; MOTOR_BUS is the only one (D-357): guarded while popup_cycle is true, motor while only window_req is, and guarded whenever both are, because a pop-up obstruction is the case that must never be retried through. none - the channel does not retry.

The Mercedes rear-SAM failure is water down a seal into a module, and the FB leaks at the cowl seam and the windscreen with the dash node sitting under both. So: every conductor enters the PMU, the dash node and each sill or rear panel from below or with a drip loop; nothing mounts in the lowest 50 mm of the footwell; the PMU's 39-way faces down or sideways and never up. Where the water actually goes when the cowl drains block is CK04, looked at with the dash out at M-1 - the rule is written now because moving a bracket then costs nothing and moving it later costs the dash.

The shielded tach core (L1-S1 6, drain to the GND bus at the dash-node end only) crosses ignition leads at 90 degrees and never runs parallel to one within 50 mm. The engine leg carries the tach past four coil and igniter leads, which is the worst run in the car. CAN2 no longer leaves the dash (D-318), so its exposure is the dash itself: the pair keeps the same 50 mm from the blower and wiper motor leads and from the O1 pop-up motor bus, and it stays twisted to the drop. Nothing else about CAN2 changes.

There is none at the module, and that is the fact to design around. The PMU-24 DL's 39 positions are all allocated: A1-A8 are the eight dedicated 0-5 V analog inputs and all eight are used; A9-A14 are configured as outputs O17-O22; A15 and A16 are the headlight and key ladders; O1-O16 are all assigned, O13 and O14 capped for the swap. There is no free input and no free output. Growth therefore never starts with a channel. It starts with: a new relay socket at the dash node - K3 and K4 now carry the release relays (D-180, D-451), so a new socket is a new part; a new branch off an existing output behind its own fuse (the way F15 / F16 / F20 / F21 hang off O12); the L3-MOD receptacle's switched feed and ground (F13) for a future dash module - the TPMS receiver D-318 wants is one such, joining CAN2 at the node's splice when it is fitted; the expander's spare pin on the DCU (P17); the ICU's unused Teensy pins (0, 1, 4, 5, 6, 38-41) with DP-ICU-B 9 as the spare input (IC17); and, for a real new channel, a second PMU in tandem (S-028: up to five). (R16, 2026-10-09)

A cavity number in this record is the number moulded into the housing itself. Read it off the part; never derive it from a drawing and never mirror it. That is a reason the DT family suits this build: the number is on the moulding, so there is no wire-side / mating-side convention to get backwards. A factory plug is different: `lands_on` carries Mazda's terminal LETTER from the factory diagram, not a cavity number, and the two never share a cell.

Every OEM junction block carries its map on the lid; here the map is derived, so it is a query and not a document (CLAUDE.md section 1 - the visual layer is a later concern and nothing else is generated). The outputs: rx7.py sql 01-electrical "select ch, name, circuit, enable_a from pins where type='output' order by ch". The fuses: rx7.py sql 01-electrical "select id, rating, location, label, feeds from fuses order by id". Printed and laminated when there is something to print with - one at the dash node, one in the glovebox beside the laptop port. Because it is a query it can never disagree with the record, which is the only reason it is allowed to exist at all.

A BAT54S is a SERIES pair - A into COM, COM into K - so a clamp built from one has exactly one correct orientation, and the record's own phrasing ('100 nF then BAT54S to 3V3 / GND') does not say which. It is this: the signal is on COM, A goes to GROUND so a negative excursion is caught by GND-to-COM, and K goes to +3V3 so a positive one is caught by COM-to-+3V3. Reversed it clamps nothing on either polarity and leaves a diode path from +3V3 to ground through the sender, which is worse than no clamp because the board looks protected. This governs every BAT54S on the ICU carrier: IC01, IC02, IC03, IC04, IC05, IC06, IC07, IC08, IC09, IC10, IC11 and IC14. Written down 2026-09-12 because the first pass of the carrier schematic had all twelve of them backwards, and the prose reads perfectly either way round - which is exactly the argument for drawing it.

Every wire is labelled at BOTH ends with printed laminated tape (Brother PT-D220, TZe-FX231 flexible-ID, 12 mm black on white), never tape-and-marker, the moment it is cut. Both ends carry the same pair, read in opposite order: from / to - e.g. O8 / L2-M-1 at the PMU end and L2-M-1 / O8 at the other; K1-87 / L2-P-3; L2-S-5 / L2-OAT-1 for a branch end; <cavity> / CAPPED for a capped far end. Wrap about 45 mm with the text outside and rub it down; where a wrap would not read, fold it into a flag. Under loom, in the bay or through a grommet: clear heat-shrink over the label. Every housing carries its code on the shell, both halves. Node labels go on the panel beside the position, from relays.label and fuses.label. (Carried from v2 install Appendix A by D-372.)

Wherever a device still has its factory plug or socket, keep it: cut it from the old harness with 150 mm (6 in) of factory lead and join each factory lead to its new wire with a sealed heat-shrink butt splice of the right size. Where a device has a stud or blade, fit a heat-shrink ring or spade terminal. The factory two-letter colour in devices names which lead gets which new wire. Nothing obsolete has to be sourced. (Carried from v2 install §4 by D-372.)

Three ways a ladder's states are told apart, one per input in inputs.decode (D-408). window - the plain case: each state is its live reading (D-142) ± inputs.window, and a reading between windows is a wiring fault. upward - for a ladder whose grounds carry load current (A4, A5: the block and the front star): an offset only ever raises a reading, so each state's window runs from (live reading − window) up to the next higher state's lower edge, the highest state up to the open threshold; nothing lands between states but a short or an open, and a misread can only be the next state up, which is always the refusing one. conductance - for a ladder fed from battery voltage (A15, A16): decode g = (k1·v − k2) / (V − v), v the input in volts, V the PMU's measured supply, k1 = 0.110 and k2 = 0.050 by design (100 kΩ bias from +5 V, 10 kΩ inside the input - the PMU's selectable 10 kΩ pull-up to +5 V, S-028 p.28, p.71; the ground-type inputs A1-A8 read 0-5 V at 10 bits and withstand 20 V, p.9), refitted at E26 so OFF reads g = 0 (k2 = k1 × the OFF reading). g is the switch's conductance in 1/kΩ and does not move with the supply: OFF 0 · ACC / PARK 0.030 · RUN / HEAD_LO 0.097 · HEAD_HI 0.219 · START 0.244 (0.214 if ACC drops in START) · PASS 0.522. Boundaries 0.015 · 0.055 · 0.150, and 0.340 on A15. The raw fault rule (0 = disconnected) still reads the input itself, and a reading more than 12 counts below the live OFF reading is a FAULT too: the switch's feed is dead with a contact closed, which the old windows read as OFF (D-410; confirm at E26 by pulling F3 at ACC and F24 at PARK, D-412). If the client cannot divide (CK15): a 2-D table of raw volts × supply volts, else fixed windows sized over 11.5-14.8 V (A16 RUN 1153-1470, START above 1490 - good only while the key sees 10.4 V or more cranking, CK14).

The cut length of every conductor is a query, never a typed number (R2): for each LIVE or CAPPED cavity in a post housing, 1.5 x its route's ft (D-202) - the cavity's own route, or its device's (devices.terminals ties the two) - and model_ft stands in, flagged as an estimate, until M-2 fills ft. The margin is the factor: no service loop is added at the bench (E20). The node conductors and the ICU / DCU tails take their routes the same way (RT13 the binnacle, RT11 the centre stack). Until the sheet check prints it, it is: rx7.py sql 02-PROJECTS/01-electrical "select c.id, c.awg, c.colour, r.id as route, r.ft, r.model_ft, round(1.5*coalesce(r.ft, r.model_ft),1) as cut_ft from cavities c left join routes r on r.id = c.route where c.state in ('LIVE','CAPPED') and c.route != '' order by c.housing, c.cav" (R10, 2026-10-09)
